sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) - AWS
sources.claim: RAG is the process of optimizing LLM output by referencing an authoritative knowledge base outside of training data before generating a response, without requiring retraining. It addresses LLM challenges including presenting false information, out-of-date information, responses from non-authoritative sources, and terminology confusion.

sources.title: End-to-End RAG Workflow - Databricks
sources.claim: RAG connects LLMs to external knowledge bases through a five-stage pipeline: ingestion, embedding, retrieval, augmentation, and generation. Retriever quality is the single biggest determinant of RAG output quality.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) - Pinecone
sources.claim: RAG is a technique that uses authoritative, external data to improve accuracy, relevancy, and usefulness of model output through four core components: ingestion, retrieval, augmentation, generation.

sources.title: Retrieval-augmented generation - Wikipedia
sources.claim: RAG is a technique that enables LLMs to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. The technique was first proposed in 2020 and has since become widely adopted in modern AI systems.

sources.title: What is retrieval augmented generation (RAG)? - IBM
sources.claim: RAG is an architecture for optimizing AI model performance by connecting it with external knowledge bases. It provides cost-efficient implementation, access to current domain-specific data, lower risk of AI hallucinations, and expanded use cases.

metadata.summary: All five sources consistently define RAG as a technique to improve LLM accuracy by retrieving external knowledge before generation. Key principles include: (1) external knowledge base connection, (2) five-stage workflow, (3) improved accuracy over training data only, (4) reduced hallucinations, (5) no retraining required.
